self_audit: Read the full ARCH file (lines 1-323) in ranges; walked every AD and CD rule plus the also_consider list (overrun, kill and reap, backoff, paging cap, 8 MiB cap, discovery, envelope vs row parse, merge, clock, namespaces, renderer exceptions, resize, snapshot write, schema bump, runs-read token). Cross-checked against adapter-contract.md, rendering-rules.md:50 and the _find_orca extract. Reported only unhandled paths.

findings.trigger_condition: A later page fails (timeout, cap, json, shape) after earlier pages succeeded
findings.guard_snippet: if page k>1 fails: SourceResult(state=PARTIAL, code=c); merge(prev, ok_pages, stopped_by_error=True); keep unread rows as not reobserved
findings.potential_consequence: Fresh pages discarded or merged as complete; freshness and PARTIAL label undefined
findings.evidence: ARCH:100 "a `SourceResult` with `ok` (bool)"; ARCH:184 "a failed cycle never calls it"; spec:7 "returns a `SourceResult` (ok, failed or partial"

findings.trigger_condition: Five sequential calls each near the per-call timeout exceed the 15 s budget
findings.guard_snippet: timeout = min(CALL_TIMEOUT, deadline - clock.monotonic()); on deadline: killpg, code=overrun, next wait measured from cycle end
findings.potential_consequence: Cycle runs up to 5x budget; overrun has no SourceResult code
findings.evidence: ARCH:106 "the cycle budget equals the interval ... at most 5 subprocesses per cycle"; ARCH:100 code set "`exit:<n>`, `timeout`, `output-cap`, `json`, `shape`, `not-found`"

findings.trigger_condition: Child goes silent but keeps stdout open; blocking chunk read never returns
findings.guard_snippet: read stdout with selectors and a deadline; after killpg join stderr thread with timeout and close both pipes
findings.potential_consequence: Collector thread hangs forever; timeout kill never fires
findings.evidence: ARCH:100 "stdout is read in chunks and the call is killed once 8 MiB is exceeded; stderr is drained on a separate thread"

findings.trigger_condition: Quit, render exception or SIGTERM while an Orca subprocess is running
findings.guard_snippet: on exit: collector.stop() sets Event, killpg(active_child, SIGKILL), reap, then restore terminal
findings.potential_consequence: Orphaned Orca child in its own session outlives the observer
findings.evidence: ARCH:106 "one daemon thread waiting on a `threading.Event`"; ARCH:100 "`start_new_session=True`"; ARCH:201 "A render exception stops the screen, restores the terminal and exits non-zero"

findings.trigger_condition: Unexpected exception in collector thread (RecursionError on deep JSON, TypeError in merge)
findings.guard_snippet: wrap each cycle in try/except Exception: publish SourceResult(ok=False, code=internal) and continue with backoff
findings.potential_consequence: Collector thread dies silently; no more polls, no error shown
findings.evidence: ARCH:201 "Adapter and parse failures become a `SourceResult` status ... they never raise into the render loop." Nothing covers exceptions outside those two classes.

findings.trigger_condition: Orca installed but probe fails, wrong version, or topics malformed
findings.guard_snippet: separate which()==None from probe failure; label FAILED (discovery); retry discovery on backoff; try/except around _find_orca
findings.potential_consequence: False binary-not-found shown permanently; malformed topics raise uncaught AttributeError
findings.evidence: extract:24 "accepts only if returncode 0 and a topic named `orca-cli`"; extract:43 line 219 `t.get(...)` is outside the try; ARCH:88 "(orca binary not found)`, and no cycle starts"

findings.trigger_condition: Orca version renames row keys; fields all unknown, extra keys hidden
findings.guard_snippet: carry unrecognised-key counts into View; inspector shows n unrecognised keys per row and cycle
findings.potential_consequence: Ledger silently all unknown; contradicts spec inspector count
findings.evidence: ARCH:112 "unexpected keys are counted per row and per cycle, not shown"; spec:38 "counted in the inspector (`n unrecognised keys`)"

findings.trigger_condition: Several rows missing dispatchId share identity (namespace, UNKNOWN)
findings.guard_snippet: if dispatchId is UNKNOWN: identity=(namespace, UNKNOWN, cycle, source_rank); never dedupe; count separately
findings.potential_consequence: Distinct workers merged as duplicates and dropped; j undercounted
findings.evidence: ARCH:112 "Row identity is `(source.namespace, dispatchId)`" and "Any other missing key becomes the single `UNKNOWN` sentinel object"; ARCH:106 j counts "distinct row identities"

findings.trigger_condition: Two dispatchIds differ only by stripped control characters, or sanitize to empty
findings.guard_snippet: key identity on the raw source dispatchId (or its hash); use sanitized text only for display
findings.potential_consequence: Different rows collide; one dropped as a duplicate
findings.evidence: ARCH:124 "`parse.py` applies it to every string from the source before it enters a `Snapshot`"; identity is built from the Snapshot dispatchId (ARCH:112)

findings.trigger_condition: hasMore null or string, workers not a list, total negative, row not an object
findings.guard_snippet: require isinstance(hasMore, bool) and isinstance(workers, list) else FAILED(shape); non-dict row counted malformed; bad total -> UNKNOWN
findings.potential_consequence: Null hasMore ends paging as complete; non-dict row crashes parse
findings.evidence: ARCH:112 "requires `result`, `result.workers` and `result.page.hasMore`; if any is missing the cycle is `FAILED (shape)`" (presence only, no type check)

findings.trigger_condition: Source key present with JSON null value
findings.guard_snippet: value = UNKNOWN if key missing or value is None
findings.potential_consequence: None reaches renderers and snapshot, breaking the sentinel invariant
findings.evidence: ARCH:112 "Any other missing key becomes the single `UNKNOWN` sentinel object ... (never `None`, `0`, `""` or `False`)"; a present null is not a missing key

findings.trigger_condition: Source JSON carries NaN or Infinity, which json.loads accepts by default
findings.guard_snippet: json.loads(s, parse_constant=reject_constant); json.dumps(obj, allow_nan=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
findings.potential_consequence: Snapshot is invalid JSON; Go reader fails to parse it
findings.evidence: ARCH:142 "`counts` (passed through as a map, never summed)" and "Output uses `json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys=True)`"

findings.trigger_condition: hasMore true but nextCursor absent, UNKNOWN, over byte bound, or starts with '-'
findings.guard_snippet: if has_more and not valid_cursor(next_cursor): stop paging, coverage PARTIAL (cursor rejected); never put a sentinel in argv
findings.potential_consequence: Sentinel reaches argv, or paging stops and reads as complete
findings.evidence: ARCH:94 "`cursor` is copied only from the previous `page.nextCursor` and byte-bounded"; ARCH:112 nextCursor is not a required key

findings.trigger_condition: nextCursor equals a cursor already used this cycle
findings.guard_snippet: if next_cursor in seen_cursors: stop paging, mark PARTIAL (cursor repeated)
findings.potential_consequence: Same page reread to cap; shown as duplicates, not a paging fault
findings.evidence: ARCH:106 "paging stops at the cap"; no repeated-cursor rule anywhere in AD-4, AD-6 or AD-19

findings.trigger_condition: Duplicate copies with equal or absent timestamps, or only one timestamp kind
findings.guard_snippet: compare liveness.observedAt else evidence.lastObservedAt; either absent: newer cycle wins, order_flag=order unknown; equal: lower source_rank wins
findings.potential_consequence: Arbitrary copy kept; spec absent-timestamp rule lost
findings.evidence: ARCH:184 "when two copies meet, the newer `observedAt` wins"; spec:44 "Either timestamp absent: the newer cycle wins and the row is flagged `order unknown`."

findings.trigger_condition: Current cycle returns a row older than the retained copy
findings.guard_snippet: keep newer values; set reobserved=True, last_seen_cycle=current, order_flag=conflict (time went back)
findings.potential_consequence: reobserved and last_seen_cycle undefined for conflicting rows
findings.evidence: ARCH:184 "the newer `observedAt` wins" and "`conflict (time went back)` when a timestamp moved backward"; reobserved is defined only for rows not returned

findings.trigger_condition: Evidence timestamp ahead of observer wall clock, or wall clock steps back
findings.guard_snippet: age = clock.wall() - last_observed_at; if age < 0: render clock skew text, never a negative age
findings.potential_consequence: Negative evidence ages render or the age formatter fails
findings.evidence: ARCH:190 "evidence age from `clock.wall()` minus `evidence.lastObservedAt`"; no rule for a negative result

findings.trigger_condition: Last good values older than 24 hours, or across a DST change
findings.guard_snippet: render as of YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS when the timestamp is not today in local time
findings.potential_consequence: Day-old as-of time reads as recent
findings.evidence: ARCH:118 "last good values shown `as of HH:MM:SS`"; ARCH:199 "displayed wall times are local `HH:MM:SS`"

findings.trigger_condition: No successful cycle yet: NOT_POLLED, NOT_AVAILABLE, or every cycle failed
findings.guard_snippet: if last_success_mono is None: render read unknown of unknown Runs since start (no successful read)
findings.potential_consequence: Header shows bare read 0; unknown rendered as zero
findings.evidence: ARCH:106 "k is its size" and "renders `read k of unknown Runs since start` when j is 0"; spec:50 "Unknown is never zero or false."

findings.trigger_condition: A row's runId becomes known after earlier cycles reported it UNKNOWN
findings.guard_snippet: track unknown-run identities as a set; remove an identity once its runId resolves
findings.potential_consequence: k+? qualifier persists after every Run is known
findings.evidence: ARCH:106 "`runs_unknown_rows`, the number of distinct row identities ... with an `UNKNOWN` `runId` seen in successful cycles since start"

findings.trigger_condition: Successful cycle after a failure streak; backoff reset rule absent
findings.guard_snippet: on success: wait = INTERVAL; on failure: wait = min(wait * 2, 60)
findings.potential_consequence: Recovered source keeps polling every 60 s, past 45 s STALE threshold
findings.evidence: ARCH:106 "After a failed cycle the next wait backs off and never exceeds 60 s (doubling from 15 s is PROPOSED)"; ARCH:238 "STALE at 45 s without a successful read"

findings.trigger_condition: Terminal resized while the Live screen runs with a fixed explicit width
findings.guard_snippet: on SIGWINCH or per redraw: re-read size, rebuild TerminalPolicy and console width, redraw immediately
findings.potential_consequence: Lines overflow or wrap after shrink; redraw waits up to 60 s
findings.evidence: ARCH:148 "Every console gets ... an explicit `width`"; ARCH:154 "a resize redraws within one cycle", and a backed-off cycle is up to 60 s

findings.trigger_condition: Interactive mode on POSIX with stdin or stdout not a TTY
findings.guard_snippet: if not (sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty()): print use --once; exit non-zero before tty.setcbreak
findings.potential_consequence: termios.error at setcbreak, or alternate-screen escapes written into a pipe
findings.evidence: ARCH:154 only gates on platform: "Interactive mode is POSIX only: on other platforms `commands.py` prints ... and exits non-zero"

findings.trigger_condition: Ctrl-Z (SIGTSTP), SIGCONT, SIGHUP, or SIGTERM arriving mid-redraw
findings.guard_snippet: on SIGTSTP: restore attrs, leave alt screen, re-raise default; on SIGCONT: re-enter cbreak and redraw; SIGHUP like SIGTERM then exit
findings.potential_consequence: Shell left in cbreak or alternate screen after suspend or hangup
findings.evidence: ARCH:154 "restores the saved attributes in `finally` and from SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers"; no other signal named, and what SIGTERM does after restore is unstated

findings.trigger_condition: UI loop blocked (slow render, file write) across two published cycles
findings.guard_snippet: write the snapshot from the collector thread per cycle, or queue every unwritten CycleResult for the writer
findings.potential_consequence: Intermediate cycles never written despite exactly-one-per-cycle claim
findings.evidence: ARCH:190 "when it sees a higher cycle number, writes exactly one snapshot for that cycle"; ARCH:106 "publishes one immutable `CycleResult` ... by replacing one reference"

findings.trigger_condition: Disk full, EXDEV temp path, temp-name collision, or permission error on snapshot write
findings.guard_snippet: tempfile.mkstemp(dir=dest_dir); fsync; os.replace; except OSError: unlink temp, count failure, show export failed, keep running
findings.potential_consequence: Orphan temp files; OSError treated as render crash, exits observer
findings.evidence: ARCH:136 "writes a temporary file and `os.replace`s it"; ARCH:201 "A render exception stops the screen, restores the terminal and exits non-zero"

findings.trigger_condition: Observer restarts; old snapshot file remains; new cycle numbers restart at low values
findings.guard_snippet: add an instance id and startedAt to the envelope; write a NOT_POLLED snapshot at start replacing the old file
findings.potential_consequence: Reader trusts previous process data; cycle number goes backwards silently
findings.evidence: ARCH:190 "publishes a `CycleResult` before the first poll (`NOT_POLLED`)" but writes only on "a higher cycle number"; ARCH:142 envelope has `cycle` and no instance id

findings.trigger_condition: Consumer validates v1.x snapshot with an older copy of the strict schema
findings.guard_snippet: ship a consumer schema with additionalProperties true; state that only the producer schema is strict
findings.potential_consequence: Every additive field breaks older validating readers
findings.evidence: ARCH:142 "the producer schema sets `additionalProperties: false`" and "Consumers reject an unknown major and ignore unknown fields"

findings.trigger_condition: snapshot.schema.json missing or invalid in the installed package
findings.guard_snippet: load and check_schema lazily inside snapshot_json or the schema test, not at module import
findings.potential_consequence: Every superclaude command fails at import via the main.py block
findings.evidence: ARCH:142 "checked with `Draft7Validator.check_schema` at import"; ARCH:82 main.py imports `superclaude.cli.observe.commands` at module bottom

findings.trigger_condition: Selected row hidden by filter or h toggle; Up, Down or Enter on an empty list
findings.guard_snippet: if selected not in visible_rows: show selected <id> hidden by filter; on empty visible_rows: arrows and Enter are no-ops
findings.potential_consequence: Inspector shows a row the list hides; index error on empty list
findings.evidence: ARCH:160 covers only a row that "disappears" from the source; filter and `h` hiding the selection, and keys on zero visible rows, are unspecified

findings.trigger_condition: result.scope.source holds a value other than flag, bound or all
findings.guard_snippet: if source not in {flag, bound, all}: render scope=<sanitized value> (unrecognised)
findings.potential_consequence: Unknown scope rendered as unbound full fleet
findings.evidence: ARCH:106 "`flag` and `all` show only `scope=<source>`, and an absent scope reads `scope unknown`"; no rule for another value

findings.trigger_condition: --once when the source is FAILED or NOT_AVAILABLE, or stdout pipe closes
findings.guard_snippet: --once exits non-zero unless state is OK; except BrokenPipeError: close stdout quietly and exit
findings.potential_consequence: Scripts read a degraded record as success; traceback on closed pipe
findings.evidence: ARCH:136 "`--once` writes `record_text` with `sys.stdout.write`"; no exit status or pipe-closure rule

findings.trigger_condition: User passes a --run value that fails the format check
findings.guard_snippet: validate --run in commands.py as a click.BadParameter before any cycle starts
findings.potential_consequence: Unspecified: silent unbound poll or crash
findings.evidence: ARCH:94 "`runId` passes a format check"; ARCH:106 "`--run` is added only when the user binds a Run"; rejection behaviour unstated

findings.trigger_condition: More than 500 rows; page cap returns a different subset each cycle
findings.guard_snippet: flag removed only when a full read (no has_more_at_stop) omits the row; else mark not reobserved without *
findings.potential_consequence: Rows flap as removed; changed-since count inflates
findings.evidence: ARCH:160 "A row is flagged `*` when it was added, removed, or ..."; ARCH:106 "paging stops at the cap"

findings.trigger_condition: Long-running observer over a churning fleet; rows never evicted
findings.guard_snippet: set RETAINED_ROW_CAP; at the cap show retention exceeded and keep counts unknown, never drop silently
findings.potential_consequence: Memory and render time grow without bound
findings.evidence: ARCH:184 "A cap on rows retained across cycles is PROPOSED"; ARCH:238 envelope lists no row-retention bound

findings.trigger_condition: One binary path talks to two Orca daemons; or namespace holds the home path
findings.guard_snippet: derive namespace from an Orca-reported instance id when verified; export a hashed namespace, not the raw path
findings.potential_consequence: Two Orcas merge rows; snapshot leaks user home path
findings.evidence: ARCH:112 "PROPOSED: the resolved Orca binary path plus the `--run` binding, or `unbound`"; ARCH:142 emits `source.namespace`

findings.trigger_condition: Stderr cut mid UTF-8 sequence at 2 KiB; stdout not valid UTF-8
findings.guard_snippet: decode stderr with errors=replace; map UnicodeDecodeError on stdout to code json
findings.potential_consequence: Decode error escapes the closed code set into the loop
findings.evidence: ARCH:100 "drained ... into a 2 KiB buffer" and "a `code` from one closed set: `exit:<n>`, `timeout`, `output-cap`, `json`, `shape`, `not-found`"

findings.trigger_condition: Implementer builds the literal set from AD-8 only
findings.guard_snippet: add cycle overran (Ns) and k duplicate rows ignored to the AD-8 literal list
findings.potential_consequence: Two spec literals have no defined owner or test
findings.evidence: ARCH:106 "the strip shows `cycle overran (Ns)`"; ARCH:184 "`k duplicate rows ignored`"; neither appears in the AD-8 list at ARCH:118

findings.trigger_condition: Source map keys (counts keys, scope keys) carry escape sequences
findings.guard_snippet: sanitize dict keys as well as values when copying counts and scope
findings.potential_consequence: Escape bytes reach screen or snapshot through a map key
findings.evidence: ARCH:124 "applies it to every string from the source"; ARCH:142 `counts` "passed through as a map"; keys not named
